conviction_note: Nothing found that the market has not seen: every load-bearing fact (Q2 1.13x book-to-bill, the raised guide, CFO's 41-42% pass-through model, falling conversion rate, peers' strong Q2 bookings) is from July/August documents. No peer has printed Q3 yet (IQVIA reports 2026-10-27), so there is no counterparty read-through on Q3 awards. The findings net to -0.6, a small negative from positioning (stock at a 52-week high, above the sell-side's ~$561 average target) and a falling backlog conversion rate. Against that sit an 8-for-8 EPS beat record, the bookings momentum management guided to, and a mild upside-paid skew. So p_up is 51 on a 13.5% absolute move, giving +0.27. The two measurements differ in sign; both are near zero and the gap is noise, not a view. This name trades on net awards, cancellations and any 2027 color, and none of those can be read before the release.

findings.finding: Bookings set-up for Q3 is constructive per primary documents. On the Q2 call (2026-07-23) management said RFPs rose substantially sequentially and year on year, expected gross bookings to ramp in H2, and called pre-backlog 'larger than backlog' and 'growing'. Q2 net awards were $795.7M (1.13x book-to-bill) against a street expectation of 0.95-1.01x. Peers that reported after Medpace confirm a firm demand backdrop: ICON Q2 gross bookings +24.1% y/y, book-to-bill 1.51 (07-29); Fortrea 1.06x, fourth quarter above 1.0 (07-29); Charles River DSA bookings +12.6% q/q (08-05). The market's bar for Q3 net book-to-bill is probably at or above ~1.1x after a +14.7% Q2 reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bookings drive this stock. Q1 2026 book-to-bill of 0.88x with elevated cancellations: -22.63% (2026-04-22). Q2 2026 1.13x against 0.95-1.01x expected: +14.71% (2026-07-22). Record Q3 2025 bookings: +9.12% (2025-10-22).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. If the market doubted the H2 bookings ramp, the stock would not be at a 52-week high, +21% since the pre-Q2 price, with the skew paying upside. What is not priced is the actual Q3 cancellation level, which management itself calls 'a wild card'. So this is a small lean, not an edge.
findings.independence: Peer documents, from different companies: ICON Q2 release https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729518057/en/ICON-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results (2026-07-29); Fortrea and Charles River via https://247wallst.com/cards/charles-river-laboratories-q2-2026-earnings-crl-01kz8ttt2xzsh2awyhsksd49wt. H1 2026 biotech VC was the strongest first half since 2022 (BioPharma Dive, https://biopharmadive.com/news/biotech-venture-capital-funding-2026-first-half/824881). All are July/August data; there is no Q3 peer print yet.

findings.finding: Revenue will fall as conversion slows, and management has said so. Q2 backlog conversion was 24.1% of opening backlog, and on the Q2 call management said '24% is kind of high relative to historical values, I would think that that is going to come down.' Backlog at 2026-06-30 was $3,014.2M, only +4.9% y/y, while revenue grew 17.2%. The 10-Q puts next-12-month conversion at $1,950-1,970M. So any 2027 color, which management said it might give 'possibly next Q', comes off a backlog that has grown much slower than revenue (the UBS backlog-coverage concern).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print, which carried the first 2026 guide: -15.9%. The 2026-02-09 reaction is the closest analogue for a forward-growth read, and the baseline does not attribute it to one line.
findings.source_date: 2026-07-2x (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30; cover share count dated 2026-07-17)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: management said it publicly and UBS has written about backlog coverage. If the market were pricing a 2027 slowdown, the stock would not sit at a 52-week high with upside-paid skew. Whether 2027 color comes on this call is uncertain.
findings.independence: The UBS (Caliendo) backlog-coverage warning is cited in a CMC Markets/investing summary (https://www.cmcmarkets.com/en-gb/opto/medp-earnings-review-medpace-stock-soars-on-bookings-beat), but the article fetched did not contain it, so it is unverified. The allmind transcript (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2933069) is the same company's statement, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print at a 52-week high ($644.73), +4.5% over 5 and 20 days and ~+21% since the pre-Q2 $531.67. That is ~15% above the late-July sell-side average target (~$561; 11 of 14 analysts at Hold). Jefferies downgraded in July saying the valuation needs book-to-bill 'solidly above 1.0x'. A high bar after a +14.7% Q2 reaction makes a merely good bookings print vulnerable. This name has fallen 15-23% on two of its last four prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last 7 reactions: +14.71, -22.63, -15.90, +9.12, +54.67, -2.32, -7.52. Median absolute move 14.7%, 3 of 7 up. Large two-way moves; beats have not protected the stock when bookings disappointed.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up and level are in the price by definition. What this finding claims is only that the bar has risen. Short interest is moderate (5.8 days, ~7% float), so a squeeze is not the counterweight; the upside-paid skew (-2.96) is. That skew argues against this finding, which is why it stays small.
findings.independence: Tape from the sealed baseline (spot, 52w-high flag, run-ups). Analyst ratings tally from MarketBeat via search: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MEDP/forecast/.

findings.finding: EPS has mechanical support. Medpace has beaten EPS consensus 8 of 8 quarters (average surprise +12.1%, per Earnings Whispers). The FY guide assumes 28.6M diluted shares and excludes buybacks after June 30. Shares outstanding fell to 27.91M at June 30 from 28.37M at Dec 31 after $294.7M of Q2 repurchases, and $527M of authorization remained. Q3 diluted shares should land below Q2's 28.55M even with no further buyback, about a 1% EPS tailwind against the $4.44-4.45 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats have not set the sign. Q1 2026 beat on EPS and fell 22.6% on bookings; the stock trades on awards.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The beat record is public, and analysts model the share count. If anything is unpriced, it is a few cents of EPS from Q3 buybacks the guide excludes. A buyback in Q3 at prices of $600+ is undisclosed until the release.
findings.independence: Beat record from Earnings Whispers via search snippet (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/MEDP). The share counts come from the same 8-K.

findings.finding: Reimbursable pass-through costs are shrinking, which mechanically caps reported revenue. They were 44.2% of revenue in Q1 and 42.9% in Q2 ($303.1M of $707.3M), and on the Q2 call the CFO modelled '41% to 42% of revenue Q3, Q4'. Direct service revenue was about $404M in Q2 (+2.4% q/q). To reach the $709-713M revenue bar at 41.5% pass-through, direct fees need about $415-417M, roughly +3% q/q. That is achievable, but it leaves little room for a large revenue beat, while margins benefit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print in the baseline is attributable to the pass-through line alone. Revenue misses have coincided with bookings misses (Q1 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: Inside what the company guided, so sized near zero. The derived direct-fee arithmetic (revenue less reimbursed OOP) is not a reported metric and is not in wire copy. If the market priced it, revenue consensus would sit below ~$705M; it sits at $709-713M.
findings.independence: CFO's 41-42% statement from the call transcript https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2933069. This shares a document with the conversion finding; it is a different line.

findings.finding: Regional biotech venture data for 2026 to date (through Q3) is weak: San Diego $1.4B raised over 113 deals through Q3 2026 (-34.1% y/y, weakest since 2022), Raleigh-Durham $184.7M (-84% y/y), per Savills Q3 2026 life-science reports. National H1 2026 was strong ($9.1B, strongest first half since 2022, BioPharma Dive). The regional series is a narrow proxy for small-biotech award flow, which is Medpace's customer base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Funding leads awards by quarters, not weeks.

findings.why_not_priced: Regional real-estate research is not on CRO analysts' screens. But it is a narrow proxy that contradicts a broader national series (H1 strong), so it is sized below that series.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative (-0.6), mainly from positioning at a 52-week high, which leans against the mildly upside-paid skew (-2.96) and goes with the run-up's high bar. Because the skew is mild and short interest moderate, p_up is held at 51 rather than below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the EPS/buyback finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, because this name trades on bookings, not EPS beats (Q1 2026 beat EPS and fell 22.6%).
Lesson 6 (inside what the company guided): pass-through finding cut from -0.4 to -0.2, because the CFO publicly modelled 41-42% for Q3.

Lesson 7 (positioning, skew): positioning negative cut from -1.0 to -0.7. The skew mildly pays upside and short interest (5.8 days, ~7% float) is moderate, not a squeeze set-up, but the sign stands against a weak skew.
Pessimism artefact note: conversion-rate finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8. Management's own statement is public and partly priced, and the set leaned negative without a Q3 document behind it.
Left standing: bookings +1.0, regional funding proxy -0.2 (already filed small, below the broader national series per lesson 5), 2027-color 0 with a wide band; abs_move 13.5 and p_up 51 unchanged.
